item.title: The Gulf Renaissance: How a New Cultural Axis Is Redrawing the Global Art Map
item.description:
Authors: harmeet singh

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: For centuries, the geography of the global art world was defined by a stable group of Western capitals—and later Hong Kong—functioning as the undisputed centers of artistic production, market liquidity, and institutional authority. Today, that geography is undergoing a structural realignment centered in the Arabian Peninsula. This paper examines the rapid emergence of the Gulf states as a new cultural axis, arguing that rather than representing a monolithic "art boom" or a simple transfer of Western institutional power, the region is developing four distinct, complementary models of cultural influence: Dubai (Commercial Gravity): Market circulation, logistical infrastructure, and global mobility. Abstract: Central sleep apnea (CSA) is a heterogeneous and relatively rare sleep breathing disorder characterized by recurrent reductions in respiratory drive and airflow during sleep. Its complex and not fully understood pathophysiology reflects challenges in respiratory control mechanisms. CSA is associated with cardiovascular, neurologic, systemic, and genetic conditions, and remains a key area for further research, particularly in improving diagnosis and understanding mechanisms. This article outlines the definition, diagnostic approaches, classification, and provides an overview of the underlying pathophysiology of CSA.
